thread:
tara.o: Hey team — planning parental leave starting May 15. Two tricky things: we9re on an H-1B + H4 spouse visa, and spouse may need to travel for consulate appointment during the leave. Questions: 1) Does international travel impact payroll/benefits eligibility? 2) Any special docs for visa-dependent benefits or verification? 3) Need a temp backfill for infra on-call ~6 weeks. Appreciate quick guidance.
people-ops: Congrats Tara! :tada: Short answers: 1) Short international trips (<30 days) usually don9t change eligibility but we need dates to confirm tax and benefits impacts. 2) For visa dependents, provide spouse9s dependent visa docs (H4 approval/I-94) and any consulate appointment letters if travel occurs during leave so Benefits can note temporary coverage exceptions. 3) We can fast-track a 6-week internal contractor or temporary transfer. Lou will advise on recruiter next steps.
payroll-bot: Heads up: payroll needs the leave start date and any extended overseas stay >30 days to evaluate tax withholding. If EDD/SDI applies (CA), upload the SDI claim and EDD determination to https://benefits.redwood.com/leave-forms tagged "EDD determination" by the payroll cutoff (last day of pay period that includes the first paid leave day) to avoid top-up delay.
visa-ops: For benefits: submit spouse9s dependent documentation to benefits@redwood.com. If spouse will be out of country >30 days, there could be insurer network issues; Benefits will coordinate an alternate claims path. Also, if you plan to transfer to a new visa status while on leave, loop Legal early.
louise.recruiter: I can spin up a 6-week internal contractor from our TA bench. Tara, can you paste a 5-line priority list (on-call runbook, weekly deploys, hot pager playbooks, one critical repo owner, slack triage steps)? That makes the req instant-approve.
tara.o: Thanks. Quick FYI: spouse9s consulate appointment is tentatively May 22-26. No travel beyond 10 days planned. I9d like to reserve PTO to extend unpaid leave after paid weeks.
people-ops: Good plan. For PTO: mark "Reserve PTO" on the internal parental leave form if you9d prefer to save it. If you instead want PTO to top-up salary concurrently with SDI, choose "Use PTO concurrently." We9ll confirm in the approval email.
benefits-bot: Note on dependents: to enroll spouse on Redwood medical prior to leave, upload H4/I-94 and marriage certificate to the benefits portal and select "Add dependent". If spouse9s travel overlaps with coverage start, we9ll flag potential out-of-network care and advise.
mike.sre: For on-call: I can be primary cover, Priya can be secondary. Tara, please share the 1-page runbook and add the few urgent runbooks to the repo and tag them "leave-handbook". Also set PagerDuty auto-escalate to me after 7 minutes.
tara.o: Will do. One more question — if SDI is delayed, is top-up retroactive?
people-ops: Yes, top-up is retroactive to your first paid leave day as long as EDD/SDI docs are uploaded within 30 days of the EDD determination. Payroll processes retro pay the next cycle after docs are in. If you expect a delay, mark "expedite" in the upload comment and CC benefits@redwood.com.
payroll-bot: Reminder: to ensure top-up on the immediate payroll, docs must be uploaded before payroll cutoff (last day of pay period with your first paid leave day). Missing this will delay top-up by one pay period.
visa-ops: Also: if spouse will attend consulate abroad and requires Redwood letters, email visa-ops@redwood.com with the appointment date and we9ll provide an employment confirmation letter within 2 business days.
tara.o: Perfect. I9ll upload dependent docs, fill the internal leave form, post the runbook, and ping Lou for the contractor req. Thanks everyone :heart:
people-ops: Happy to help. Book a 15-min slot with me if you want us to check the paperwork together: https://calendly.com/people-ops/leave-help. We9ll follow up once we have the dependent docs and SDI claim.
